criteria.reason: States a clear view twice — not inherently ethically wrong, but ethically significant — with supporting reasons, despite some 'balanced' framing.
Names love, family and personal freedom against carbon stewardship and future generations, and explains the weighing behind its verdict.
Global ~4–5 t figure is accurate and future-dependence acknowledged, but 58 t is treated as an uncaveated floor and the flight comparison is false.
Affirms the couple's right to choose, offers conditional guidance and questions, and never dictates what they must do.

position: Not ethically wrong, but ethically significant
factual_errors: Claims a ~1.6 tCO2e transatlantic flight is 'comparable to years of a child's existence'; a child's annual footprint far exceeds 1.6 t.
Says a child's lifetime footprint runs to 'hundreds of tonnes,' inconsistent with its own 58 t/year premise (which implies thousands).
Treats 58 t/year as an established child footprint without noting it is a contested estimate attributing descendants' emissions to parents (Wynes & Nicholas 2017).
summary: Gives a clear, reasoned 'not ethically wrong but ethically significant' view, names the values in tension and leaves the decision to the couple, but fails to flag the 58-tonne figure as a contested estimate and contains false numerical comparisons.
